# Interpretation — issue #823, round 1 (analyzer)

**Task:** Does the per-context map h predict the model's own output or context-side processing? (external-answer refit, #779 substrate). Parent #722; substrate #779. Status: `interpreting`; upload-verification PASSed.

---

## 0. Data verification (spot check)

Seed 42 → contexts 3867, 2193, 3271, 445, 2165 pulled from the raw completions on HF (`issue823_own_vs_external/raw_completions/`). All five match the arm definitions: A′ = the model's own regenerated answer to the context's question; B2 = Sonnet plain answer to the same question (different text, same content target — text cosine to A′ mean 0.489, only 9.6% of pairs >0.8, so B2 is not a paraphrase); B1 = Sonnet "weird"-style answer (visibly off-distribution: logP under own model −3.51 vs A′ −0.47); C = derangement — another context's A′ answer teacher-forced under this context (checked against `derangement_seed42.json` permutation: the C answers visibly answer *other* contexts' questions). One style covariate noted for later: B2 answers are markdown-heavy (headers/bullets) relative to A′. `phase0_verify.json`: bundle sha256 matches, 5000×28×3584, revisions pinned (bundle `c94070508aa1…`, lmsys `200748d9d3…`).

**Verdict: spot check PASS** — arms are what the plan says they are; headline numbers below are trustworthy modulo the caveats in §4.

## 1. Fact sheet

**Design (one line).** Ridge map h: context-side activation `cx_last(x)` → answer-span mean activation `v_s(x)`, GCV λ, 5-fold CV (KFold shuffle, seed 0), 28 layers × 3584 dims, Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct, n=4998 LMSYS contexts (common valid set). Read-out layers pre-registered from #779: evil L14, sycophancy L26, hallucination L17. Four refit arms (A′/B1/B2/C); arm A (the #779 bundle) used for the reproduce gate only. Transfer = fit on A′, score on B1/B2/C (per plan).

**Refit pooled fold R² at read-out layer** (mean over 5 folds):

| trait (layer) | A′ own | B2 Sonnet-plain | B1 Sonnet-weird | C derangement |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| evil (L14) | 0.599 | 0.585 | 0.472 | +0.004 |
| sycophancy (L26) | 0.608 | 0.556 | 0.468 | −0.008 |
| hallucination (L17) | 0.626 | 0.591 | 0.506 | +0.007 |

**Pre-registered decision stats** (Δ = A′ − B2; Bonferroni α=0.017; `falsifier_artifact` False for all traits):

| trait | Δ(A′−B2) pooled-fold | boot CI (per-context estimand) | paired-t p_bonf | Cohen d | verdict (pre-registered rules) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| evil | 0.0142 | [0.0175, 0.0270] | 0.356 (NS) | 0.89 | **H3** |
| sycophancy | 0.0521 | [0.0504, 0.0615] | 0.0012 | 4.85 | **H1** (Δ>0.05 ∧ R²_C<0.05) |
| hallucination | 0.0349 | [0.0404, 0.0506] | 0.014 | 2.55 | **H3** |

B2−C is enormous everywhere: 0.564–0.585, boot CIs [0.506, 0.531] and up, p_bonf ≤ 2e-6. A′−C likewise (0.595–0.619). H2 (context-side only, all arms within ±0.03) is rejected in the direction of content mattering: C collapses.

**Transfer (fit=A′, score at read-out layer):** →B2 0.457/0.451/0.461 (≈74–76% of A′'s self-fit; ≈78–81% of B2's own refit); →B1 ≈0 (−0.070/+0.050/−0.059); →C strongly negative (−0.744/−0.653/−0.803).

**Trait-agnosticism (load-bearing for interpretation).** The per-layer refit and transfer fold curves are numerically identical across the three traits — the ridge fit is one trait-agnostic map per arm; "trait" enters only through the pre-registered read-out layer. The per-layer own-output increment Δ(A′−B2) is U-shaped in depth (layers 0–6: +0.030; 7–13: +0.016; 14–20: +0.021; 21–27: +0.034; Spearman(layer, Δ)=0.05, p=0.82 — no monotone trend). The three read-out layers sample this one curve at Δ(L14)=0.014, Δ(L17)=0.035, Δ(L26)=0.052.

**Validity diagnostics** (`validity_diagnostics.json`): logP under own model — A′ −0.47, B2 −1.70, C −2.70, B1 −3.51 (B1 is the off-distribution diagnostic by construction; C is fluent text, just content-mismatched). Activation-target similarity cos(v_B2, v_A′) at read-out: 0.927/0.953/0.922. Answer lengths: A′ mean 320 tokens, B2 244, B1 279.

## 2. Interpretation (what h is)

1. **h predicts context-content processing, not primarily the model's own output.** A content-matched answer written by a different model (B2) is 93–96% as predictable as the model's own regenerated answer (0.556–0.591 vs 0.599–0.626), while the model's own fluent text under the *wrong* context (C) is indistinguishable from zero predictability at fold resolution (−0.008 to +0.007). Since C is on-distribution text (logP −2.70, better than B1's −3.51) and A′-vs-C differ only in context–answer match, the collapse isolates content match — not fluency, not authorship — as what h carries.

2. **A small, real own-output increment sits on top.** Δ(A′−B2) is positive under both estimands for all three traits (per-context boot CIs exclude 0 everywhere: even evil's [0.0175, 0.0270]). But it is 6–12× smaller than the content-match effect (B2−C ≈ 0.56–0.58), and part of it is a length artifact: |Δlen(A′,B2)| correlates with the per-context R² gap (Spearman 0.067/0.108/0.056, all p<1e-4; A′ answers average 320 tokens vs B2's 244), and in the matched-length stratum (|Δlen|≤25, n=3063) the gap shrinks ~15–30% to 0.0155/0.0481/0.0385.

3. **The per-trait H1/H3 verdicts are depth facts, not trait facts.** Because the fit is trait-agnostic, sycophancy's H1 label means "at L26 the own-output increment is 0.052"; evil's H3 means "at L14 it is 0.014". The pre-registered rules were applied faithfully and sycophancy nominally crosses the 0.05 threshold (Δ=0.0521, boot CI [0.0504, 0.0615], p_bonf=0.0012) — but the margin over threshold is 4%, and the matched-length stratum estimate (0.0481) sits below it. Honest read: a graded own-output increment that varies with read-out depth and shades sycophancy/L26 toward H1, not a categorical difference between sycophancy and the other traits.

4. **Transfer sharpens the picture.** The A′-fit map carries most of its skill to B2 unrefit (0.45–0.46) — the content representation is shared across answer sources. It carries nothing to B1 (≈0) even though a *refit* on B1 reaches 0.47–0.51 — the weird style shifts the map's coordinates but not the recoverability of content. And it *anti*-predicts C (−0.65 to −0.80, far worse than predicting the mean): h's predictions are context-specific enough to be systematically wrong for a mismatched answer — itself direct evidence that the map encodes the context's content.

5. **What this means for the #722/#779 line.** #779's R²≈0.6 "h predicts v(x)" result is now decomposed: ≈93–96% of it is available from any content-matched answer; only a 0.014–0.052 sliver (layer-dependent) is specific to the model's own text. Downstream uses of h as a "what the model will say"-predictor should be reframed as "what an answer to this context looks like in activation space".

**Suggested headline (for the eventual clean-result title):** "The context→answer-activation map is ~94% content-matching, not self-prediction: external content-matched answers score R² 0.56–0.59 vs own-answer 0.60–0.63, and content-mismatched own text collapses to R²≈0 (MODERATE confidence)."

Confidence suggestion: MODERATE — single model, single corpus (LMSYS slice), tier-3 synthetic external answers (Sonnet-written), n=4998 but 5-fold/1-seed fit, and the H1/H3 boundary is threshold-sensitive.

## 3. Statistics discipline notes

- **Two estimands, both reported (resolves the "point outside CI" anomaly — caveat #5).** The Δ point estimates are differences of *pooled fold R²* (SS-weighted, SS_tot on the test-fold mean); the bootstrap CIs resample the *equal-weighted per-context R²* gap (rng seed 0). These are different estimands, so evil's point 0.0142 sitting below its CI [0.0175, 0.0270] is a mixed-estimand presentation artifact, not a computation bug: the per-context gap means (0.0223/0.0561/0.0454) sit inside their CIs for all three traits. Verified in code (`run_823.py` computes `delta` from pooled fold means; bootstrap over per-context arrays) and numerically. Recommendation for the body: label each column by estimand; never pair the pooled-fold point with the per-context CI in one sentence.
- The paired t over 5 folds (df=4) is the pre-registered *secondary*, low-power test; the context-level bootstrap is primary. Evil's NS t-test with a CI excluding zero is the expected low-power behavior, not a contradiction.
- C ≈ 0 is stated as "indistinguishable from zero at fold resolution", not as an affirmed zero — fold SDs put ±~0.01 around it.

## 4. Caveats and provenance (pre-registered items 1–6)

1. **Harness reproduce gate PASS.** Arm A (bundle) refit reproduces #779 at read-out: R² 0.5991/0.6058/0.6262, |Δ| vs #779 ≤ 0.0015. The refit harness is the #779 harness.
2. **A-vs-A′ drift — qualify H1 as "own *regenerated* output".** cos(v_A, v_A′): evil L14 0.9898, hall L17 0.9894 (both soft-WARN < 0.99), syco L26 0.9936; R² deltas ≤ 0.0022. The A′ arm regenerated answers (same prompts, same decoding recipe) rather than reusing bundle text; residual sampling drift means every "own output" claim here is about the model's own *regenerated* answers, not the exact #779 strings. The ≤0.0022 R² impact bounds the consequence as negligible for the verdicts.
3. **Phase-4 dedupe patch (commit `d68455ce60`).** The rescored pipeline dedupes the phase-4 ridge loops (3780→700 fits) and rescores transfer from the A′ refit predictions; the fast Gram-eigh solver FAILED full-size parity and the canonical solver is the default — headline numbers come from the canonical path.
4. **OPEN CONCERN `phase5-length-r2-valid-idx-mismatch` — BINDS, but only kills a diagnostic; rescued inline.** `validity_diagnostics.json.length_r2_correlation` is `{}` because phase 5 sliced the 5000-length span arrays against 4998-length compacted per-context R² arrays; `scipy.stats.pearsonr` raised on the length mismatch and a bare `except Exception: logger.warning(...)` (`run_823.py` ~L2140–2200) swallowed it. **No reported headline number is corrupted** — the block is an isolated diagnostic — but the pre-registered length-confound check was silently missing from the artifact. I recomputed it inline with correct alignment (`span[common_valid_idx]`): Spearman(|Δlen|, per-ctx gap) = 0.0671/0.1082/0.0556 (p = 2e-6/2e-14/8e-5) and the matched-length stratum results in §2.2. The silent-swallow is a fail-fast violation worth a code follow-up; the artifact-side hole should be named in the clean-result.
5. **Bootstrap CI anomaly — root-caused, artifact not bug** (see §3, two estimands).
6. **Measurement validity framing.** This is the read-out/prediction regime (all-layer fit, pre-registered read-out layers from #779 — no post-hoc layer selection; no selection-symmetric-null concern per plan §456). Per-comparison constructs: A′−B2 = own-output specificity of h (proxy: pooled/per-context R² gap between own-regenerated and content-matched external answers, teacher-forced activations — on the natural token positions of each answer, but B1/B2/C are teacher-forced *by design*, so claims are about *predictability of activations under teacher-forcing*, not about on-policy generation of external text; the #432→#456 caution applies to reading these as behavioral claims, which this task does not do). B2−C = context-content match (proxy: same map, matched-source answers with matched vs deranged contexts). A′/B1/B2 vs C is the plan's processing null — the plan substituted arm C for the body's per-arm fit-level shuffle null (see §5).

## 5. Planned-vs-actual

- **4 refit arms, not 5.** Arm A (bundle answers) was used only for the reproduce gate; refit arms are A′/B1/B2/C — per plan (arm A′ supersedes A as "own answers" to control decode-recipe drift).
- **n=4998, not 5000.** Common valid set after per-arm validity filtering (2 contexts lost to non-finite A′ logP; `common_valid_idx.json`); all arms scored on the identical context set.
- **Body's per-arm fit-level shuffle null not run.** The body's DV 1 listed a shuffle null "still run per arm as the floor"; the approved plan replaced it with arm C as the processing null. Reference prior: #779's shuffle null was R²≈0.12; C lands at ≈0.004–0.007, *below* that floor, so no verdict depends on the substitution — but the clean-result must state the deviation.
- **Plan's identity baseline (predict v_s from v_A′ directly) not computed.** Partially covered by the activation-cosine diagnostic (cos(v_B2, v_A′) ≈ 0.92–0.95, which bounds how much of B2's predictability could come through target similarity alone) — flag as a missing planned cell in the body per check-11b discipline.
- **`length_r2_correlation` diagnostic missing from artifact** (caveat #4) — rescued inline; numbers in §2.2/§4.4.
- **28 zero-span B2 rows** in the valid set have zero target vectors (0.56% of contexts) — negligible dilution of B2's R², direction conservative (would shrink B2, i.e. inflate Δ, by at most ~0.006).
- **Scope caveats:** external answers are tier-3 LLM-generated (Sonnet), single external source; B2's markdown-heavy style is a residual covariate between A′ and B2 alongside length; single model, single context distribution.

## 2. Interpretation (what h is)

1. **h predicts context-content processing, not primarily the model's own output — demonstrated for a plain-style external source.** A plain-style content-matched answer written by a different model (B2) is 91–98% as predictable per-trait (mean ≈94%) as the model's own regenerated answer (0.556–0.591 vs 0.599–0.626), while the model's own fluent text under the *wrong* context (C) is indistinguishable from zero predictability at fold resolution (−0.008 to +0.007). Since C is on-distribution text (logP −2.70, better than B1's −3.51) and A′-vs-C differ only in context–answer match, the collapse isolates content match — not fluency, not authorship — as what h carries.

2. **The retention claim is plain-style-specific; style carries a nontrivial share.** B1 is *also* content-matched, yet refits at only 0.468–0.506 (77–81% of own) and receives ≈0 transfer from the own-answer map — so "any content-matched answer retains the accuracy" is NOT supported. The distinct style costs ~0.09–0.13 refit R² even with content held matched, and B2 shares surface style with A′ (both plain prose; B2 additionally markdown-heavy). Alternative explanation carried explicitly: part of B2's high retention may reflect style similarity to the model's own answers rather than content match alone. The C collapse still bounds the style-only account — fluent own-model style with mismatched content predicts nothing — so content match is necessary; the open question is how much of the A′↔B2 gap-closure is style-assisted.

3. **A small, real own-output increment sits on top.** Δ(A′−B2) is positive under both estimands for all three traits (per-context boot CIs exclude 0 everywhere: even evil's [0.0175, 0.0270]). But it is ~9–23× (per-context) to ~11–41× (pooled) smaller than the content-match effect (B2−C), and part of it tracks a length covariate: |Δlen(A′,B2)| correlates with the per-context R² gap (Spearman 0.0671/0.1082/0.0556, p = 2.1e-6/1.8e-14/8.4e-5; A′ answers average 320 tokens vs B2's 244).

4. **The sycophancy threshold call is marginal — the length-matched sweep straddles 0.05.** The pre-registered rules were applied faithfully and sycophancy nominally crosses (Δ=0.0521, boot CI [0.0504, 0.0615], p_bonf=0.0012). The matched-length stratum analysis is **post-hoc** (the plan pre-registered only the length correlation, not a stratified re-estimate). Across |Δlen| cuts the sycophancy per-context gap is: ≤10 → 0.0525 (n=2829), ≤25 → 0.0481 (n=3063), ≤50 → 0.0490 (n=3295), ≤100 → 0.0498 (n=3772), ≤200 → 0.0521 (n=4330), full sample 0.0561 — it STRADDLES the 0.05 threshold with no privileged cut. Evil and hallucination at the ≤25 cut read 0.0155 and 0.0385 (both stay on their side of the threshold). Because the fit is trait-agnostic, the per-trait verdicts are depth facts, not trait facts: sycophancy's crossing means "at L26 the own-output increment is ~0.05", evil's non-crossing "at L14 it is 0.014". Honest read: a graded, depth-dependent own-output increment that shades the L26 read-out toward the threshold — not a categorical difference between sycophancy and the other traits.

5. **Transfer sharpens the picture.** The A′-fit map carries most of its skill to B2 unrefit (0.45–0.46) — the representation is shared across the two plain-style answer sources. It carries nothing to B1 (≈0) even though a *refit* on B1 reaches 0.47–0.51 — the distinct style shifts the map's coordinates but not the recoverability of content. And it *anti*-predicts C (−0.65 to −0.80, far worse than predicting the mean): h's predictions are context-specific enough to be systematically wrong for a mismatched answer — itself direct evidence that the map encodes the context's content.

The reading was correct AND the reviewer found a sharper mechanism the implementer had not: on a re-run, `results` is loaded ONLY from the main checkpoint, whose results files are immutable once collected — so the pending set recomputes the ORIGINAL main-dispatch residue R0 every run. Rows that already succeeded (and were BILLED) in a prior run's `redrive1`/`redrive2` checkpoints are never merged back; those dirs are counted for numbering only, never re-loaded. So every re-run RE-BUYS them. It also traded away a case the pre-fix code handled: a crash mid-retry leaves an orphaned batch completing server-side while the re-run submits the same rows again — double-billed on success. And the halt message's claim that a re-run "resumes completed rows and re-submits the remaining rows" is false of the current code: resume covers only main-checkpoint completions and the re-submitted set is a SUPERSET of "remaining", while the digest reports the smaller current residue.

MAGNITUDE, grounded by the reviewer rather than left scary: transport class is `{rate_limited, transport_exhausted}` only (empty-response rows are NOT redriven, and no response-validity predicate is passed, so the billed-invalid-response loop shape does not exist here); batch-errored/expired/canceled rows are unbilled server-side, so billing recurs only via the R0 re-buy. Pathological (org outage expires the whole batch): R0 approximately 15k, so each re-run re-buys up to about $35-70 per 24-48h SLA cycle. Existing bounds: 2 rounds per run, the ~24h SLA throttling loop rate, no mechanical auto-relauncher keyed on exit 3 (the watcher re-drives only `no_compute_available`), and billing only on succeeded rows.

RULING: NOT blocking the in-flight production dispatch/harvest — run 1 is semantically correct, because on a first run R0 IS the current residue and within a run the pending set shrinks correctly. The defect executes only on a SECOND exit-3-driven run, which is operator-initiated.

## How this surfaced

The fixed-code smoke resume completed rc=0 and its digest read `ok=47/48 error=0 redrives=0 regen_personas=[]`. rc=0 plus `error=0` would normally read as clean. It is not: 47 of 48 is one row unaccounted for, so the digest was opened rather than trusted.

`validity_counts_by_persona` shows persona 6 as `{"ok": 1, "empty": 1, "n_rows": 2}` — every other persona all-ok. The row's own metadata: `context_id=14`, `persona_idx=6`, `arms=[8]`, `validity='empty'`, `filled=False`, `answer_text=None`, `cap_hit=False`, `regen=False`, and decisively **`stop_reason='refusal'`**.

## Why the stop_reason changes the interpretation

1. NOT transient. A refusal is a content decision on a fixed (persona, question) pair at temperature 1.0 — re-submitting the identical request is not expected to recover it. Retrying is futile, so no retry policy fixes this.
2. CORRECTLY not retried today. The retry class is `{rate_limited, transport_exhausted}` only; `empty_response` maps to validity `empty` and is deliberately excluded. That exclusion is right — but it means refusals flow straight into the validity accounting and then into the mask.
3. NOT missing-at-random, and the missingness is on the MANIPULATED VARIABLE. Refusals are persona-correlated by construction: a persona's framing is what triggers them. So dropout is correlated with exactly the factor under study.

## The design already defends the differential-mask confound

The plan's mask is the INTERSECTION across arms: new common-valid = parent common-valid ∩ validity of all 5 arms. So a refusal on any single (context, persona) pair drops that CONTEXT from EVERY arm, keeping arms mutually comparable. There is no per-arm differential mask. That protection holds and is not in question.

## But the plan's drop ARITHMETIC does not survive this rate

The intersection is what makes the rate dangerous rather than benign. Roughly 3 distinct (context, persona) pairs exist per context at the registered nesting (14,996 pairs / 5,000 contexts). At a per-pair refusal rate p, the probability a context loses at least one pair is about 1-(1-p)^3.

At the smoke's point estimate p ≈ 1/48 ≈ 2.1%: about 6.1% of contexts drop ⇒ roughly 300 contexts of 5,000 ⇒ n_common ≈ 4,700 and about 300 new invalid rows PER ARM.

Plan v10 expects approximately 10 new drops (n ≈ 4,990) and its registered mask-integrity kill fires above 50 new invalid rows per arm. So the projected figure exceeds the abort threshold by roughly 6x. The failure mode is the expensive one: the full ~14,996-call wave is paid for and the fit phase then aborts on mask integrity.

Also affected: the `realized_train >= 3584` check. At n_common ≈ 4,700 the single-split training slice still clears d, so that rung survives — the mask kill is the binding constraint, not the estimator-regime floor.

## Statistical caveat on the estimate (stated, not hidden)

The estimate rests on ONE refusal in 48 draws. The 95% interval on 1/48 runs roughly 0.05% to 11%, so the true rate could be low enough for the plan's arithmetic to hold, or several times worse. That uncertainty is the reason to pilot rather than either dismiss it or re-plan on it. A single observation is enough to justify measuring; it is not enough to justify a design change.

## Action: PILOT-GATE the production wave

Consistent with the standing convention that a large judge wave is pilot-gated before production dispatch (~100-200 draws at the exact production instrument), the same logic binds a 14,996-call GENERATION wave. Ordered: a larger smoke at the exact production instrument to estimate the refusal rate with a usable interval, then gate the production dispatch on the projected drop count against the registered mask kill.

Decision rule for the gate: project drops as 1-(1-p_hat)^3 over 5,000 contexts and compare to the >50-per-arm kill. If the projection clears the kill with margin, dispatch production. If it does not, the round needs a registered decision BEFORE spending — the candidate levers, none of which may be chosen silently: raise the mask-kill threshold with a stated scope caveat about non-random dropout; drop the offending persona(s) from the roster if refusals concentrate in a few; or accept a smaller n_common and re-check every rung's estimator regime against d. Raising a threshold to make a run pass is the paper-over move and requires the caveat to be carried into the result, not buried.

## The defect

The regeneration path dispatches ONE BATCH PER PERSONA, SERIALLY, each waiting for its own batch to complete before the next persona begins. Verbatim from the 300-context pilot log (`/tmp/823-pilot300.out`):

    19:56:20 Assignment verified: 896 distinct (context, persona) pairs
    19:56:20 dispatch_calls route: N=896   -> msgbatch_01AK2F13X8yzQuLqy2LciSe3
    20:03:46 Cap-hit trigger: persona 0 has 12 over-cap rows — re-generating at 2048 tokens
    20:03:46 dispatch_calls route: N=12    -> msgbatch_01Mf8otQLeosDvqqDKG9bHto
    20:07:16 Cap-hit trigger: persona 1 has 7 over-cap rows
    20:07:17 dispatch_calls route: N=7     -> msgbatch_01UBK2GiZmNxbmjebi6KEXeK
    20:12:41 Cap-hit trigger: persona 2 has 2 over-cap rows
    20:12:41 dispatch_calls route: N=2     -> msgbatch_01LVzHwo1vR9ybPrCB6XgFxe
    20:16:10 Cap-hit trigger: persona 3 has 3 over-cap rows
    20:16:11 dispatch_calls route: N=3     -> msgbatch_01RxpNozv4LHbnUzE1zCPFjf
    20:18:24 Cap-hit trigger: persona 4 has 1 over-cap rows
    20:18:25 dispatch_calls route: N=1     -> msgbatch_01Kv4UmnykGFBkPyoszBQdBT

Five separate submissions inside 15 minutes and still climbing the roster. 16 personas ⇒ 16 SEQUENTIAL batch round-trips. At pilot scale each tiny batch clears in ~3-5 min; at production scale every submission is subject to the Batch API's 24-hour service window, so this can serialize into a day or more of pure waiting ON TOP OF the main wave. This is the serial-inner-loop throughput failure the project has a standing rule against.

Diagnostic note on how it was found: six distinct batch ids appeared in the log for what should have been ONE sub-batch (896 calls at chunk size 1,000). Chunking was ruled out by reading the dispatcher's chunk constant; the cascade shape 896 -> 12 -> 7 -> 2 -> 3 -> 1 with a `Cap-hit trigger: persona N` line before each one identified the path. Neither the offline test suites nor any of the three code reviews caught this — it is a wall-clock property of the realized dispatch sequence, not a property of any single function, so only a real pilot at non-trivial scale exposes it.

## The fix (Fix D, relayed to the live fix round)

Keep the TRIGGER per-persona — the >2% threshold is correctly evaluated against each persona's own row count and that semantic must not change. POOL the DISPATCH: evaluate the trigger for every persona first, take the UNION of over-cap rows across all personas that tripped, submit ONE regeneration dispatch. One batch, one wait.

Carried constraints: the checkpoint dir becomes a single pooled one instead of the per-persona dirs — which also SIMPLIFIES the regen residual documented-but-not-fixed in the previous round (one quarantine remedy instead of per-persona); per-persona accounting must survive pooling (digest per-persona regen fields, per-record `regen` flag, per-record `max_tokens` must still identify persona and cap — pooling the transport must not pool the bookkeeping); a test must assert exactly ONE dispatch occurs with a submitted id set equal to the union.

## The dropout is PERSONA-driven, and concentrated

Per-persona refusal rates: p06 "Edmund Hartley" 12/37 = 32.43%; p10 10.53%; p04 5.41%; p11 5.26%; p01 2.00%; p02 2.67%; p00 1.00%; and NINE of sixteen personas at exactly 0%. Top four hold 80% of all refusals. p06 alone is 48% of them and a 3x outlier over the next worst.

Structural note: personas 4-7 appear only from k>=8 and 8-15 only in k=16, so a high-index persona's refusals delete contexts from EVERY arm through the common-mask intersection. One pathological high-k persona silently deletes ~6% of the corpus for all arms including k=1.

## NO in-scope lever clears the gate — measured counterfactuals

    full roster            19/300 = 6.33%  ->  317 contexts   KILL FIRES
    drop p06                7/300 = 2.33%  ->  117 contexts   KILL FIRES
    drop p06,p10            7/300 = 2.33%  ->  117 contexts   KILL FIRES
    drop p06,p10,p04        6/300 = 2.00%  ->  100 contexts   KILL FIRES
    drop p06,p10,p04,p11    6/300 = 2.00%  ->  100 contexts   KILL FIRES

Roster surgery is INSUFFICIENT. Even removing the four worst personas leaves 2x the threshold. So the >50/arm criterion is incompatible with real refusal behavior on this corpus at n=5000 REGARDLESS of roster composition.

## The diagnosis: the kill criterion's SEMANTICS are wrong, not its number

The >50/arm gate exists to catch a BROKEN PIPELINE — capture failures, missing rows, a mis-staged store. Refusals are not a pipeline fault; they are expected model behavior on a real-world corpus. The gate currently CONFLATES "the rig broke" with "the model declined", which is why it is simultaneously too tight for refusals and (arguably) the right shape for integrity faults. Those two want different thresholds AND different dispositions: an integrity fault should kill; refusal attrition should be REPORTED, bounded, and carried as a scope caveat.

That is a design defect in a registered criterion, so it routes to the planner + critics — NOT to an orchestrator threshold edit. Raising a gate so a run passes is the paper-over move; the auto-continuation rule for a self-defeating plan is explicit that a hyperparameter must not be descoped to dodge a contradiction.

The correct claim carries a qualifier: **no LADDER-PRESERVING exclusion clears the gate.** The clearing path lands on exactly 50 — zero headroom, one additional refusal re-fires it — and gets there only by excluding p00 and p01, which destroys the k=1 and k=2 rungs (below). ## CORRECTION 2 — roster exclusion is CONFOUNDED WITH THE MANIPULATED VARIABLE (new, and the stronger argument)

Verified from the pilot's own `assignment.json`: under the registered rule `persona(i, k) = i mod k`, arm k uses exactly personas {0..k-1}.

    k=1  -> {0}                k=2  -> {0,1}            k=4  -> {0,1,2,3}
    k=8  -> {0..7}             k=16 -> {0..15}

The ladder's independent variable IS the number of distinct answer-origin personas. So excluding persona p shrinks EVERY arm with k > p:

- excluding p06 leaves k=8 with 7 personas and k=16 with 15 — the rungs stop being the rungs they are labelled;
- excluding p00 DESTROYS k=1 outright (its only persona) — the ladder's baseline anchor.

Roster surgery is therefore not merely insufficient; it perturbs the very quantity under study. It cannot be the fix. The artifact records this per counterfactual as `arms_shrunk` / `arms_destroyed` / `changes_manipulated_variable`, so a future reader cannot re-propose the lever without seeing the confound.

## The amendment: one gate becomes three dispositions

v10's single `> 50 new invalid rows per arm` mask-integrity kill conflated a BROKEN PIPELINE (its design intent) with EXPECTED MODEL REFUSALS, and the 300-context pilot proved it unsatisfiable by any ladder-preserving adjustment. v11 splits it, classifying every new-invalid row by its persisted `stop_reason` (never the validity label, which undercounts refusals 19 vs 25):

1. **Pipeline-integrity kill** — > 50 NON-refusal invalid rows in any arm ⇒ abort. Threshold UNCHANGED, now scoped to the fault class it was built for. Pilot measured 0/896 in this class.
2. **Refusal-attrition budget** — refusal-attributed context drops ≤ 500 ⇒ REPORT per (persona × arm) + a population scope caveat carried into `## Takeaways`. Derived from the pilot's Wilson 95% upper bound (484) plus headroom, and CEILINGED by P1 well-posedness: 4998 − 500 = 4498 ⇒ per-fold n_train ≥ 3598 > d = 3584. The estimator boundary caps the budget, not the wish to pass; the point estimate (317) clears at 1.6× margin.
3. **Residual attrition kill** — TOTAL drops > 500 ⇒ abort. The budget is not a blanket pass.

Also amended: generation cap 1024 → 4096 with ONE 8192 regen round and convergence RE-MEASURED (the pilot's cascade terminated with the trigger still exceeded — "regen ran" is never read as "resolved"); full roster KEPT with p06 retained; and the downstream arithmetic throughout (n_common ≈ 4683, per-fold n_train ≈ 3747, dof cap now expected bindable rather than a tail case, P2 top rung ≈ 3372).

## Codex found that round 4's fix DEFEATS round 5's fix

Concern `p0-checkpoint-reuse-not-keyed-on-verifier-schema`. Verified at source before
acting:

`cached_verify` in `run_p0_verify` reuses a per-persona entry when
`ent["file_sha256"] == file_sha[p]` and `ent["n_failures"] == 0`, returning
`[], {(i, p) for i in ent["context_ids"]}` WITHOUT calling
`p0_verify_persona_records`. The entry stores only
`{file_sha256, n_records, n_failures, context_ids, verified_at}`, and the outer
checkpoint key is the GENERATION fingerprint — model, temperature, caps,
roster/template hash, context pin, mask-gate schema. Nothing in either key describes
the P0 VERIFIER's own schema.

So a checkpoint written by the round-4 verifier — which used `isinstance(x, int)` and
would have recorded `n_failures: 0` for a `context_id: true` record — is honored by the
round-5 verifier. The reuse branch rebuilds the seen pair from cached context ids plus
the integer bucket, so the boolean never reaches the new `type(x) is not int` check at
`:1182-1183` and the gate can still PASS. **Round 4's checkpoint (BLOCKER 4) bypasses
round 5's schema fix (BLOCKER 2).** Two independently-correct fixes that interact
destructively — neither reviewer could have seen it from one round alone.

Currently unreachable in practice (no checkpoint exists anywhere — verified earlier this
round), but it becomes live the moment P0 runs once and any later verifier change lands.
That is precisely the shape that survives to bite a future session.

`EPM_LONG_PHASE_HEARTBEAT_FRESH_MIN` window, so fresh markers keep the verdict HEALTHY.
Skip the heartbeat on a 24-hour phase and the task both goes unobserved AND becomes
eligible for a forbidden re-spawn. Genuine session death is covered by the watcher's
crash-recovery pass, not by a cron this status must not carry.

## What I did

sb1 read `processing=1000, succeeded=0` for 1 h 25 m on the congested `batch` org (93
in-flight batches / 521,829 requests). I concluded it was not draining, cancelled it,
re-pointed its checkpoint entry at idle `low_prio`, and resubmitted 1,000 calls.

The cancelled batch then ended: **`succeeded: 997, canceled: 3`**. It was ~minutes
from completion. The `succeeded: 0` I kept reading was a LAGGING counter, not a stalled
batch.

## The inferential error, precisely

In the same turn I made the decision, I had ALREADY observed that `succeeded` is an
unreliable progress signal — I wrote that `high_prio` showed "0 succeeded across
136,256 processing requests" and noted my own 14 sub-batches went 0-succeeded → done
without my sampling any intermediate value.

I then used that observation to JUSTIFY overriding my own pre-stated threshold. That
inverts it. The correct inference from "my drain signal is unreliable" is:

> I cannot measure whether sb1 is draining, therefore I have NO evidence of a stall,
> therefore the free-path rule stands and I wait.

Instead I promoted an unreliable signal's null reading to positive evidence of
non-drain. **An unmeasurable quantity is not a measured zero.**

This is the same class as this morning's misread (a 0/48 batch read as latency rather
than capacity), in the opposite direction — and the threshold I set explicitly to
guard against impatience is exactly what I talked myself past. The supporting
evidence I cited (10 of 11 same-submission siblings done; org congestion asymmetry)
was real but consistent with "sb1 is last in a deep queue and nearly finished" — which
is what it actually was.

## Cost, and why I am NOT attempting recovery

- ~1,000 calls duplicated on `low_prio` (~$2.3 against a ~$35 wave — ~7%).
- 997 completed generations on the cancelled batch are billed and orphaned.

The 997 ARE retrievable (Anthropic retains results ~29 days) and could be merged, then
only the 3 canceled requests re-run. **Declining that:** it needs hand-written merge
code writing foreign results into the driver's own results-file format plus a
synthetic 3-request sub-batch — fiddly work OUTSIDE the driver's reviewed path, on the
harvest that feeds the whole downstream store, to save ~$2.3. The risk of corrupting a
13,996-row verified-clean harvest exceeds the saving by a wide margin. Accepting the
duplicate spend is the cheaper and safer call.

No correctness impact: generations are sampled at temperature > 0, so the fresh 1,000
are as valid as the discarded 997 — same model, same params, same prompts, one wave.
Provenance unchanged.

Recording this because the realized wall deviates far past the ≥2× threshold that
mandates a basis update in the same turn, and because the same defect propagates to
every remaining row of the §9 table.

|---|---|---|---|
| P-Cap + P-Store (rows 2+3) | 4.5 + 0.4 = **4.9 GPU-h** | **459 s** (7 min 39 s; 16:23:42Z → 16:31:21Z) | **≈38× over-booked** |

**Measured per-unit basis, from the producer sidecars** (this is now the currency for
any further capture-class sizing on this task): persona group p00, 5,000 pair rows,
`elapsed_s = 115.48` ⇒ **43.3 rows/s** at batch 8 / 28 layers / hidden 3,584. Over the
realized 14,996 rows that is **≈346 s of capture compute**; the remaining ~113 s of the
459 s wall is model load + the one-commit 6.02 GB P-Store upload.

**Why the plan was wrong, mechanically:** P-Cap is a TEACHER-FORCED single forward pass
over ~15k short sequences with a span-mean reduction — no generation, no sampling loop,
one pass per row. On an H100 that is minutes. The §9 row was an ASSERTED figure, not a
measured pilot through the production entrypoint, which is exactly the basis class
`.claude/rules/plan-compute-sizing.md` forbids for a >~15 min phase.

**Consequence for P-Fit, and what I did NOT do.** The 1.5 GPU-h P-Fit row inherits the
same unmeasured-basis defect, so I am not treating it as a wall estimate in either
direction. I did **not** substitute a guessed fence — the #1092 lesson (a guessed
`timeout 3000s` killed a healthy ~25 min/cell run) cuts against invented fences
symmetrically. Instead the plan's own **G3 gate is the fence, and it is already the
correct instrument**: at unit 1 it measures the realized per-cell wall through the
production entrypoint at production shape, projects `per_cell_s × total_units`, and
takes the designed abort (`rc=6`, `fits_abort_report.json`) only if the projection
exceeds `FITS_WALL_ABORT_FACTOR (2.0) × planned_wall_h` — 3.0 h, or 7.0 h under the
priced `--force-canonical` contingency. That is a measured-pilot fence with a plan-
registered constant, so I launched at the default rather than overriding it; changing a
plan-registered gate value without approval would be an unapproved scope deviation. If
G3 does abort, its report carries the measured `per_cell_s` and re-derivation proceeds
from that number, not from the plan's.

A `[phase=done]` arriving ~38× early against a phase with an explicit "All persona
groups already checkpointed — skipping capture (upload only)" resume branch is the
false-DONE shape, so the completion was treated as a claim to verify, not a result.

   is precisely P-Gen's pair-level invalid count — not a round number, and not a

## Diagnosis: the shipped gate implements SUPERSEDED v10 semantics

The mask itself is not a surprise. `mask_n` 4629 against `parent_valid_n` 4998 is
exactly the 369-drop mask already verified and cleared at P-Gen time (v129), and 369 is
**within** the plan's own 500-context total-drop budget (admissible window [484, 517],
plan lines 640-645). What fired is a PER-ARM gate, and arithmetically a 369-context union
spread over 5 arms cannot leave every arm under 50 — so an undifferentiated per-arm gate
at 50 was unsatisfiable the moment that mask was accepted.

Plan v13 already knows this and forbids the shipped form. Binding text:

- **line 1175** — the kill is `count of integrity-class (non-refusal) NEW invalid rows per
  arm vs 50`, "keyed on persisted `stop_reason` (**never validity labels** — pilot: labels
  undercount refusals 19/25)", and "pilot measured **0/896** integrity-class".
- **line 549** — "v10's undifferentiated > 50-per-arm gate would have halted on e.g. 60".
- **line 590** — the class-scoped form "supersedes the single > 50-per-arm abort, whose
  semantics the 300-context pilot [showed wrong]".
- **lines 1196-1200** — "> 50 gate's semantics wrong: it **conflated a broken pipeline
  with expected model refusal behavior**"; the required behavior is halt-and-report with
  **per-arm per-class** drop accounting.

The shipped code does neither. At `scripts/issue823_ladder_fits.py` lines ~994-1018,
`pair_ok(i, p)` judges validity as `inputs.store_span[p][j] > 0` — a **span-length
validity label**, precisely the signal the plan says never to key on — and

file exactly once in a load-bearing sense (line ~1393) and only inside the M3 descriptive
digest, never in the gate.

this exact failure mode. It is a plan-adherence defect, not a threshold that needs
relaxing and not evidence the data cannot support the fit.

The drops are **non-monotonic** in ladder rung: k8 (344) exceeds k16 (224), while

## The result that is NOT the headline but may matter more — a dissociation

The own/plain anchor arms have catastrophic R² (≈ −8.5 to −10.8) yet retrieval acc@1 ≈ 0.21-0.26, roughly **200× chance**. The maps preserve neighborhood identity while being wildly mis-scaled / mis-centered. Per-context ECDFs put ~78-81% of anchor-arm contexts below R² = −2, so this is distribution-wide, not a few outliers. This is exactly the R²-vs-retrieval dissociation the project's identity-baseline + kNN rule exists to surface: R² alone would have called these maps worthless.

## Mechanism — the decline is mostly a MECHANICAL mixture penalty

The implied mixture penalty computed from between-persona target variance tracks the observed drop closely: at k16, implied 0.171 vs observed 0.156 (L14); implied 0.192 vs observed 0.202 (L26). The mechanical floor accounts for essentially all of the decline. The fixed-k1-denominator re-read falls more steeply (k16 L14 0.272 vs 0.345 own-denominator), consistent with denominator inflation plus residual growth rather than map degradation per se. So "mapping quality degrades as personas are mixed" is TRUE as measured, but the decline is largely what mixing targets mechanically forces — not evidence that the map itself becomes harder to learn. That distinction must survive into the clean-result; it is the difference between a trivial and a substantive reading.

| | L14 | L26 | L17 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ss_res ratio pooled/reference | 1.310 | 1.303 | 1.305 |

The common-denominator R² gap is ~0.15 — essentially the whole headline pooled drop
(0.156 / 0.202 / 0.150) — while the denominator moves only 5–6%. Monotone in k at every
layer: ss_res ratio 1.10–1.17 (k=2, n=2,186) → 1.19–1.27 (k=4, n=1,223) → 1.25–1.28
(k=8, n=615) → 1.30–1.31 (k=16, n=310).

Representativeness: the k=1 arm's own mean `ss_res` on each shared subset is 0.947–0.990 of
its mean over the whole 4,629-context mask — a typical slice, not an easy one.

**Offset-bias control.** With `v_j(x) = m(x) + p_j` and persona 0 as reference, a shared map
differing only by a constant offset predicts an excess of `||p_bar||² ≈ E/k`, where `E` is
the between-persona mean-shift energy already in
`ladder_analysis_summary.json → mixture_floor.implied_mixture_penalty`. Measured excess is
3.4–12.8× that and the discrepancy WIDENS with k (3.4× at k=2 → 12.3× at k=16), the opposite
of the offset mechanism's prediction; it instead tracks the FULL energy `E` (0.73–0.80 of E
at k=8 and k=16). All 12 arm×layer cells return
`excess-tracks-full-between-persona-energy`.

(`n_train_per_fold` [3703, 3704] vs `d` 3584) with `g2_parity_gate.pass: false` and
`sensitivity_dof_capped: null`. Near interpolation a ridge can nearly fit its training
targets including persona offsets, which then generalize as noise; a well-conditioned fit
(n >> d) would average those offsets into the intercept and pay only ≈ E/k. So this
degradation may be specific to the near-interpolation regime rather than a structural
property of the map. Falsifiable prediction: at larger n/d, `measured_excess / E` should fall
toward 1/k. Testing it needs dimensionality reduction or more contexts and is NOT in scope
here.

## Question

Does the answer-origin effect survive a well-conditioned fit, or is it an artifact of the
interpolation threshold?

The `inconsistent-origin-persona-ladder` round plus its denominator-free paired re-read
(`shared_persona_paired.json`, git main @ `84633d46c6`) established that the mixed-origin map's
held-out squared error is ~30% higher than the single-origin map's ON IDENTICAL TARGETS — not a
denominator effect, and not the shared-map-plus-constant-offset effect either (measured excess
is 3.4–12.8× the `E/k` that offset predicts, tracking the full between-persona mean-shift energy
`E` instead).

The one confound left standing: those fits sit at `n_train_per_fold` 3,703 vs `d` 3,584, i.e.
`n/d = 1.033`, the interpolation threshold. Near interpolation a ridge can nearly fit its
training targets INCLUDING their persona offsets, which then generalize as pure noise. A
well-conditioned fit would instead average the offsets into the intercept and pay only ≈ `E/k`.

**Pre-registered prediction to test:** as `n/d` grows, the ratio
`measured_excess / E` falls toward `1/k`. If it does, the effect is a near-interpolation
artifact and the paper's new sentences need to be walked back to the mechanical reading. If it
holds flat near 0.73–0.80, the origin effect is real and the caveat in
`app:origin-ladder` can be dropped.

## Shape (planner owns the final numbers)

- **Extend, do not redo.** The existing 5,000-context ladder generation and capture stay valid;
  this round adds contexts from the same #722 LMSYS pool under the SAME registered assignment
  rule `persona(i, k) = i mod k` and the same 16-persona roster (`roster.json`), so the existing
  rows are a prefix of the new set.
- **Two arms suffice, not the full 5-rung ladder.** The decisive contrast is k=1 vs k=16. For
  those two arms the unique (context, persona) pair count is ~1.94 per context (1 when
  `i mod 16 == 0`, else 2), versus 3.0 for the full ladder — roughly a third off the generation
  bill. The intermediate rungs k=2/4/8 already exist at n=5,000 and are not what the prediction
  turns on.
- **Target `n/d`.** `d` is 3,584. `n/d ≈ 5` needs ~18,000 train rows/fold ⇒ ~22,500 contexts;
  `n/d ≈ 10` needs ~45,000. Planner picks the rung set; the read wants at least three points to
  see a trend, e.g. n/d ≈ 1 (banked), 2.5, 5, and 10 if affordable.
- **Primary read: an n-ladder of the paired statistic.** At each `n/d` rung, recompute the
  shared-persona paired `ss_res` comparison (`scripts/issue823_shared_persona_paired.py`, git
  main @ `d526008c67` — REUSE it, do not rewrite) and plot `measured_excess / E` against `n/d`
  with `1/k` drawn as the reference line. Shared-persona contexts scale with the corpus:
  ~1,400 at 22,500 contexts versus 310 today, so the CIs tighten by roughly 2×.
- **Free side-benefit:** this finally answers the minimum-contexts half of the original
  follow-up ask, withheld in the parent round when the solver-parity gate failed and the
  dimension-boundary rung turned out unrealizable at the realized mask (train rows 3,336 < 3,584).
- **Estimator hygiene is the point of the round, so it is not optional:** report
  `n_train_per_fold`, `d`, `n_over_d_ratio`, the per-fit selected λ and dof, and the G2
  solver-parity gate at EVERY rung. The parent round's `g2_parity_gate.pass` was false and
  `sensitivity_dof_capped` was null; both must be resolved here rather than carried forward.
  Pure-GCV λ selection below the dof cap is refused per `.claude/rules/gotchas.md`.

## Cost character (planner re-sizes; this is the dispatch-time estimate)

- **Generation:** ~22,500 contexts × ~1.94 unique (context, persona) pairs ≈ 44,000 Claude
  Sonnet calls at the parent round's settings (temperature 1.0, `max_tokens` 4096). Route through
  the Anthropic Batch API per `.claude/rules/llm-judging.md`; PILOT-GATE it, since it clears the
  ~5,000-call threshold. This is the dominant cost of the round and it is API spend, not GPU.
- **Capture:** ~44,000 teacher-forced forward passes through Qwen-2.5-7B at the 4 captured
  layers — batched, order 2–5 GPU-h on a single H100, well under the 20 GPU-h rail.
- **Fits:** vectorized ridge at 4 rungs × 4 layers × 5 folds. At `n/d = 10` the Gram-side solve
  grows; size it against `.claude/rules/vectorize-many-cell-fits.md` and measure a 1-cell pilot
  at production shape before projecting a wall.
- Refusal yield: the parent's 300-context pilot measured 93.7% per-context survival with
  refusals persona-concentrated (p06 alone 48% of them). Budget the same shortfall and
  re-measure rather than assuming it carries.
